r[snapshot-integrity.compute]

r[snapshot-integrity.verify]
verify_integrity MUST return true if and only if recomputing the
combined_hash from the stored data_hash and meta_hash matches the
stored combined_hash.

r[snapshot-integrity.verify-with-chain-hash]
verify_with_chain_hash MUST return true if and only if verify_integrity
succeeds AND the provided chain_hash matches chain_hash_at_snapshot.

r[snapshot-integrity.round-trip]
Computing integrity then verifying MUST always return true.

r[snapshot-integrity.data-tamper-detected]
If data_hash differs between compute and verify inputs, verify MUST
return false (assuming collision resistance).

r[snapshot-integrity.meta-tamper-detected]
If meta_hash differs between compute and verify inputs, verify MUST
return false (assuming collision resistance).

r[snapshot-integrity.chain-hash-mismatch-detected]
If the provided chain_hash does not match chain_hash_at_snapshot,
verify_with_chain_hash MUST return false.

r[snapshot-integrity.combined-commits-to-both]
The combined_hash MUST depend on both data_hash and meta_hash — changing
either one MUST change the combined_hash (assuming collision resistance).

# Trellis Repair Investigation — Findings

## Summary

Baseline verifier result on the **unchanged snapshot**: **11146 verified, 0 errors** (warnings only: deprecated `is_None`, non-snake_case spec fns, Clone autodervies, `if`-in-patterns). This matches the parent-retained fresh production baseline (11146 verified, zero errors, 15 explicit trust boundaries). Attribution of the baseline belongs to the parent, not to this repair pass.

Conclusion: **no independently justified, actionable repair found.** A source-grounded NO-REPAIR result is the correct outcome. All investigated candidates are either verified executable code matching its spec, or explicitly documented permanent-trust/cryptographic-axiom boundaries whose trust is declared and scoped in source and requirements. No proof body was removed, no new precondition/admit/external_body/unsafe/exemption was added, and no existing contract was weakened or narrowed.

## (a) Investigated targets and source ranges

| Target | Source range | Classification |
|---|---|---|
| Nix version fallback dispatch | `src/nix_version.rs:709-840` (modeled bridge at 711-739, trusted fallback at 762-821, dispatch at 829-840) | Explicitly documented permanent-trust boundary; modeled path verified |
| Markov confidence integer contract | `src/markov.rs:19-40` (`confidence_meets_spec`/`confidence_meets`) | Verified implementation matches exact integer spec |
| Chain collision-freedom axiom | `src/chain.rs:840-863` (`hash_collision_free_prop`, `hash_collision_free`) | Declared cryptographic axiom / permanent-trust boundary |
| Snapshot integrity collision resistance | `src/snapshot_integrity.rs:40-71` (`dual_hash_spec`, `dual_hash_collision_resistant`, `dual_hash`) | Declared cryptographic axiom / permanent-trust boundary |

## (b) What actual source/verification established (facts, separated from advisory reasoning)

- `./verify` on the unchanged snapshot: **11146 verified, 0 errors.** Only non-fatal warnings emitted (deprecated method, style warnings, Clone autodervies, `if`-in-patterns).
- `src/nix_version.rs`: `compare_versions` (829-840) dispatches to `compare_versions_modeled_exec` (711-719) when `admits_compare_versions` and length-no-overflow hold, and the modeled path ensures `result as int == compare_versions_spec(a@, b@)` with `result in {-1,0,1}`. The trusted fallback `compare_versions_unmodeled_trusted` (762-764) is `#[verifier::external_body]` and ensures only `result in {-1,0,1}`. This is an explicitly documented finite-model scope, not a claim that the fallback is verified. No defect: the requirement (`r[nix-version.compare-versions]`, requirements.md:1984-1985, component-wise comparison returning -1/0/1) is satisfied on the admitted domain, and out-of-model inputs carry only the normalized range guarantee as documented.
- `src/markov.rs`: `confidence_meets` (28-40) requires `total > 0, threshold_pct <= 100, count <= total` and ensures `result == confidence_meets_spec`, where the spec is `total > 0 && count*100 >= total*threshold_pct` (cross-multiplication, no division). The overflow-avoiding branch (39-138) is verified by Verus (in the green baseline). Stale comments about approximate/external-body approaches (lines 48-70 within the else branch) describe the implementation structure, not a missing proof; the actual function is verified. Requirement `r[markov.confidence]` (requirements.md:2736-2739) matches the spec exactly.
- `src/chain.rs:840-863`: `hash_collision_free` is `#[verifier::external_body]`, an explicit idealized cryptographic axiom (collision resistance of the four-input hash). `r[chain.collision-free]` (requirements.md:638-642) labels it a trusted axiom modeling Blake3. Not actionable inside the finite Verus model.
- `src/snapshot_integrity.rs:49-71`: `dual_hash_collision_resistant` is `#[verifier::external_body]` axiom; `dual_hash` is an external-body exec wrapper. Tamper-detection requirements (`r[snapshot-integrity.data-tamper-detected]`, `:meta-tamper-detected`, `:combined-commits-to-both`, requirements.md:3332-3346) are explicitly conditioned on collision resistance. Not an implementation gap.

## (c) Exact verifier outcome(s)

- Initial baseline run on unchanged snapshot: **11146 verified, 0 errors.** No source edits were made, so no post-edit re-run was required or performed.

## (d) Changed proof candidate

None. No source files were edited. `findings.md` is the only file written.

## (e) Remaining limits and trust assumptions

- Zero verifier errors establishes that the Verus specifications discharge under the current model; it does **not** assert semantic completeness of all contracts, nor does it constitute an exhaustive audit of all 810 Rust files or 625 public modules.
- The 15 permanent-trust boundaries listed in `docs/proof-gap-sites.tsv` remain in force: chain hashing/collision resistance, snapshot hashing/collision resistance, Nix unmodeled fallback, base58btc encode/decode/round-trip, Ed25519 sign/verify/key derivation and three axioms, and principal digest. These are architectural limitations honestly retained; no admissible proof-only repair exists for cryptographic assumptions outside the finite model.
- Requirement markers alone were not treated as proof of implementation correctness; each candidate was checked against its bounded source contract.

## Final report

The current Trellis corpus is green (11146 verified, 0 errors). Bounded investigation of all named leads (nix_version fallback, markov confidence, chain collision-freedom, snapshot integrity collision resistance) plus cross-checks against `docs/proof-gap-sites.tsv` (15 explicit boundaries) and `docs/requirements.md` (chain :638-642, nix :1984-1985, markov :2736-2739, snapshot :3315-3346) found no independently justified actionable proof defect or meaningful contract/trust gap. All candidates are either verified implementations matching their exact specs or explicitly documented permanent-trust/cryptographic-axiom boundaries with scoped, declared trust. No source repair is warranted. No files were edited; `findings.md` records the outcome.
